newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-GAME ABANDONED AFTER BOTAFOGO LEFT WITH SIX PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GAME ABANDONED AFTER BOTAFOGO LEFT WITH SIX PLAYERS.

text.p: Defending champions Botafogo ended a melancholic Brazilian championship campaign five minutes early at the weekend after four of their players were sent off and a fifth collapsed injured.
Botafogo had been reduced to seven men, were trailing 4-1 to Portuguesa and had just had a penalty awarded against them when winger Mauricinho fell to the ground clutching his leg in the 85th minute.
The referee waited 10 mintues before abandoning the game as a 4-1 win for Portuguesa. Under the rules, Botafogo had too few players to continue, having already used all their permitted substitutes.

Botafogo were down to nine men by the start of the second half after having Franca sent off for a violent tackle in the first half and central defender Wilson Gottardo dismissed during the break for arguing with the referee.
Souza and Otacilio were given their marching orders in the protests which followed the penalty award. Rio de Janeiro newpapers on Monday accused Mauricinho of pretending to be injured.
The win gave Portuguesa a place in the quarter-finals of the championship on the day the first stage came to an end.
Botafogo, who sold most of the team which won the title last year, finished 17th.

Goias, who beat Gremio 3-1 away, also went through to join Cruzeiro, Palmeiras, Guarani, Atletico Paranaense, Atletico Mineiro and Gremio, who had already made sure of their places in the play-off stage of the tournament.
Goias overtook Sport Recife, who lost 4-1 to Palmeiras, and Internacional, who missed a penalty and had defender Regis sent off as they lost 1-0 to bottom club Bragantino.
Fluminense, one of Brazil's most traditional clubs, joined Bragantino in the second division, despite beating Vitoria 3-1.
Criciuma and Bahia, who started the weekend one point ahead of Fluminense, both won away.

Bahia beat Flamengo, Fluminense's local rivals, 1-0 in Rio de Janeiro where a lone Fluminense fan on the terraces was attacked, beaten and chased out of the ground by Flamengo supporters at the end of the game.
Flamengo had Fabio Baiano and Fabiano sent off, while striker Romario, playing his third game since rejoining the club on loan from Spain's Valencia, missed two good chances and looked out of shape.
Criciuma came from behind to beat Atletico Paranaense 2-1 away.
